dossier.public_summary: The dips are not the same from one orbit to the next: every second dip is much shallower, and each orbit looks different in depth compared to the next. The signal is carried by a couple of deep, outlier events.

reasons.why: Odd transits are ~6x deeper than even with >5 sigma difference, classic signature of an eclipsing binary folded at half the true period (24.4 d in this case), not two similar planetary transits.
Single-transit depths are wildly inconsistent; top 2 deep outliers carry almost the signal, indicating few strong dips rather than a steady planet transit.

Depth appears to change by >100% between sectors, and sector_depths_by_source confirms differs_by_source (TESS-SPOC 741 ppm vs QLP 2469 ppm), supporting variable-depth binary/blend rather than a planet of fixed depth.
reasons.value: 0.0009912 depth_change_pct 103 (sector 54 741 ppm err 395, sector 81 2233 ppm, sector 92 2683 ppm)

reasons.why: Independent ML scorer rates this as much less planet-like than the median planet, agreeing with other false-positive indicators.
